Calling any one with Art Skills!! We need you!
My last placard for the maternity events was designed and drawn by my kids. But there are so many people with better skills who could help create powerful messaging for pictures I hope will go into national newspapers.
Please could you create placards- these can be small or big and on the back of recycled car (cereal boxes/delivery boxes)
The message is simple…
Labour can’t be rerouted 
Babies Can’t Wait 
How many mums have to suffer? 
Anyone who has laboured would never accept 90 minutes as acceptable?
Keep our mums and babies safe 
Distance costs lives
Every minute matter in an emergency
Birth experience matters. 
Or create your own!
I know as a community there will be people who want to be involved but may be housebound or not want to attend the peaceful protest in Barnstaple Square next Saturday (7th Nov) at 2pm. Whole are gathering to show their support to the families who have been affected, and continue to be affected by the maternity closure.
For me it’s not just maternity (which is bad enough).
The strategic movement of services away from NDDH to Exeter and the inequality people NDDH supports now face.  
If you are not aware.
Alex ward has been closed at NDDH.
ENT has been moved to Exeter.
Pathology has moved to Exeter (and it can’t cope will volume of samples so private companies are now processing these samples- and at what cost?!)
Ambulances are now being re routed in certain postcodes to Exeter not NDDH.
Exeter is not big enough to support this number of people. Everyone suffers.
So I am asking you a personal favour.
Firstly, if you can and you care about this please join me for an hour at 2pm next Saturday 7th November in Barnstaple Square. Show the trust, the council and the government that, when it matter a community can unite and organise to say ‘no, this is not acceptable’
Help us gain nation media attention that people can’t ignore. An attitude of ‘it won’t make a difference’ is why services have been eroded because they know people are conditioned to not stand up and that they can get away with it with out a fuss. 
10,000 people standing in that square would get national attention. Please do your bit and help by standing in solidarity with your community. We all need the hospital. We all have connection to people giving birth- whether it’s your mother, your sister or your daughter. 
This affects everyone. 
People keep asking how can I help?
1. Like and Share this post (this spreads the message further in the fb algorithms)
2. Tell other people about the event (7th Nov 2pm Barnstaple Town Square)
3. Give an hour of your time to move your feet and attend the event. This helps get an incredible picture for national news and shows how many rope care. It’s not enough to talk behind closed door. Something visual like this shows how many people care.  
If, like me, you never considered yourself a ‘protest’ person, I was just like you before this year. 
I thought protests were just about people standing around. Or, even causing trouble. This event is organised by intelligent people, who have already formed a scrutiny committee to hold the trust accountable. It is not people who want to cause trouble. It is people coming together to stand shoulder to shoulder with families and say ‘we see you. You are important. We we fight for you to have the best possible birth experience’
How many fathers have now missed the birth of their child because they couldn’t get there in time? 
How many mothers have dealt with things alone because family and friends couldn’t visit because they were looking after other kids at home(and the journey was too far)?
How many mothers have been pushed out before they were ready? 
How many parents have been forced to take their newborn in a car (over the recommended minutes for a newborn) to make the journey home exhausted?)
How many women have now travelled the further distance by car during contractions and active labour?
How many have had babies delivered in A And E with non specialist staff or midwives?
How many A And E doctors have suffered stress by trying to managed a woman in labour alongside the unpredictability of a normal  A and E shift?
How many women have travelled home post c section when (trust me ) you feel every bump, swerve and brake? 
This suffering must stop. We are not a third world country. Maternity services are essential. Leadership of the trust step aside and let someone else solve this problem if you can’t. 
Stand with these women and families. See you on Sat 7th November Barnstaple Town Square 2pm.

The SNP's position on data centres.
Scotland must embrace the artificial intelligence revolution or risk missing out on its economic potential, the [SNP](https://www.heraldscotland.com/topics/snp/?ref=au)'s AI minister has warned.
Writing for the Herald on Sunday, Alyn Smith said he wants Scotland to become the "natural place" to create and grow technology businesses, generating "real jobs in the real world".
The minister also likened sceptics of artificial intelligence to people who would have dismissed the lightbulb as "a dangerous anti-candle device".

records.bodyText:
Forres SSEN substation granted planning approval by Moray Council.
The existing substation was described by SSEN at a meeting of Moray Council's Planning and Regulatory Services Committee as "constrained", prompting the need for a new facility in the same location.
Planning permission has been granted for a new substation to be built outside Forres.
Corshellach Substation, operated by Scottish and Southern Electricity Network (SSEN), will be built next to the existing Berryburn Extension substation 12km south of Forres.
The newly-approved facility will connect the proposed Clash Gour Windfarm, that surrounds Berryburn Windfarm, to the national grid.
The substation plans have received no objections and no local representations opposing construction, and have now been approved subject to conditions.
The meeting included a presentation from SSEN representatives, questions from councillors, before a final agreement to grant the planning permission.
The environmental impact of the substation was addressed, as due to construction, 1.05 hectares of already felled trees will not be replanted.
— in Forres.

records.bodyText:
The historic Musselburgh and District Electric Light and Traction Company tram line opened on 12 December 1904 running from Joppa (connecting to Edinburgh's cable-hauled trams) to Levenhall.
The route expanded further east to Tranent Road in Cockenzie (5 August 1909) and Port Seton (31 December 1909), creating a total single-line route of 6.55 miles.
Edinburgh Corporation took over operation of the line as far as Levenhall in 1931, running Service 21 from the Post Office (G.P.O) to Levenhall.
The eastern section from Levenhall to Port Seton closed on 25 February 1928 and was replaced by motor buses. The remaining service to Levenhall operated until 13 November 1954.
Portions of the old track and double-track loops—such as a section near Morrison's Haven—have occasionally been uncovered during road or maintenance works.
Musselburgh Power Station (Commissioned 1904) Musselnburgh & District Electric Light & Traction Co. Trams commenced Dec 1904. 3xPeache Steam Engines (140HP/95Kw) Type Gc. The power station provided power supplies up to 1948.
In later years this site became the South of Scotland Electricity Board's Musselburgh depot before being sold to a developer for housing in the 1990's. (Thanks to John Bygate)— in Musselborough.

records.bodyText:
Plans  have been lodged with the council for underground cabling which will connect a second wind turbine near Dales Voe to the grid.
The cable will run from the Luggie’s Knowe site to the local electricity distribution system near to the A970/Ladies Drive.
Shetland Aerogenerators received planning consent in late 2024 for a 150-metre tall wind turbine and a battery energy storage system, with a total generating capacity of nearly 20MW.
It came after a first turbine there, slightly smaller in size, was installed in 2015.
The latest planning application says the length of the proposed cabling is around 2,700 metres, with the 33kV cables buried at a minimum depth of around 80cm.
It is expected that cable works could begin in February, with energisation targeted for August.
Work is ongoing to prepare land near to the A970 for a new substation which will connect to the planned eight-turbine Mossy Hill wind farm and host electrical switchgear for SSEN.
Meanwhile a construction environmental management plan, submitted to the council earlier this month, said that construction on access tracks for the turbine development should start at the end of the year.
Construction on the turbine is expected to last for around 12 months.
When planning permission was approved for the second Luggie’s Knowe turbine, Shetland Aerogenerators said it was exploring routing community benefit payments into schemes such as Hjaltland Housing Association’s existing fuel vouchers programme.
It said the 5MW turbine alone could produce enough energy to power more than 2,600 Shetland homes annually, while the battery system “will offer flexibility improving network capacity and accelerating Shetland’s transition to net zero”.
Shetland Aerogenrators also operates the five-turbine Burradale wind farm outside of Lerwick, and is developing plans for eight turbines and battery storage on a site next to Sullom Voe Terminal.— in Shetland.
